sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Two dry-season image reviews followed by a limited non-intrusive instrument traverse

**Instrumentation:** Orthographic image comparison, differential surface profile, shallow ground-penetrating radar, paired broadband magnetometers, and an off-site regional reference logger

**Study boundary:** A coded upland pattern field containing discontinuous rectangular relief, exposed stone, and saturated margins.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Surface form:** Repeated right-angle edges and short parallel rises remained visible under different soil-moisture conditions but did not form a complete wall or drainage plan.

**Radar response:** Three shallow planar reflectors followed the strongest surface edges and ended abruptly within otherwise uniform substrate. No continuous void was resolved.

**Magnetic response:** Two stationary packages recorded the same low-amplitude broadband pulse sequence during one traverse. The sequence was absent from the regional reference instrument and did not recur the following day.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations retained:** Historic extraction, frost-sorted ground, collapsed shallow workings, transient electromagnetic interference, and instrument coupling remain plausible.

**Unresolved point:** The paired magnetic packages agreed in timing and amplitude despite separate power and logging systems. One event is insufficient to assign a continuing field source.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Incomplete geometric surface pattern with limited shallow reflectors and one unassigned locally correlated magnetic event

**Action:** Preserve non-invasive baselines and repeat only with a regional reference package operating before site arrival.

**Field restriction:** Excavation, marking, and unattended instrumentation are not authorized by this record.
